findings.reason: a node sent to serve.py:2067 lands in the discovery cache, not the reader §5 asks it to change, wasting its first read and inviting an edit to the wrong function.
findings.text: §5 cites `readiness_state` at `reckon/serve.py:2067` and, at line 114, `_read_readiness_state` at `serve.py:1794` and `_plan_record`'s `read_state` call at `reckon/metadata_index.py:593`; at the reviewed tree these resolve to serve.py:2167, serve.py:2160 (call site 1894) and metadata_index.py:666 respectively — `serve.py:2067` is `_cache_discovery_result` and `metadata_index.py:593` is inside `_row_for`, so §5, which runs after §2–§4 rewrote serve.py and metadata_index.py, points its node at the wrong functions by construction

findings.reason: the ten-parse bound is unreachable as stated because the index build adds a parse per plan, and reaching it requires editing `reckon/metadata_index.py`, which §5's write paths (roadmap.py, serve.py, the test) omit, so the node either fails its own gate or writes outside its scope.
findings.text: §5's done-when asserts that the metadata index build's per-plan parse ("`_plan_record` calling `_plan_html.read_state` … `reckon/metadata_index.py:593`") "reads through the same memo", but at the reviewed tree `_plan_record` (metadata_index.py:645) reads the file itself (`text = path.read_text(...)`) and calls `_plan_html.read_state(text)` directly at line 666, and its own docstring (lines 656–659) states the read is deliberately "the file's own, not the memoised text parse_meta shares"

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — three line anchors in §5 no longer resolve in the tree a node will read.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §5's done-when is a counting bound (at most ten `read_state` parses over ten plans across a cold roadmap read and a discovery read) and names a declared negative control (with `read_authored` restored to its own parse under its own kind, the count exceeds ten).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §5's evidence is a committed test (`tests/test_every_plan_read_is_memoised.py`) plus the roadmap/audit test results, none of it on a scratch or node-local path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the symbols §5 names (`read_state_and_text`, `section_authored`, `readiness_state`, `read_authored`, `_plan_record`, `_audit_plan_state`) are mechanism-named and exist; no plan label, ticket number or version tag reaches a symbol or comment.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §5 asserts the metadata index build's per-plan parse "reads through the same memo", but the cited code reads the file itself.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §5 carries one deliverable: the plan-parse memos are unified so one parse serves every reader.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §5's text ("runs after §3, which writes roadmap.py, and after §4, which writes serve.py") agrees with followup f-araiid-002 ("§5 after §3 and §4"), and both modules it names are written by those nodes.
